body:
## Problem

During the 2026-09-20/21 GLM-5.3 trial (OpenCode native runtime, metered Friendli endpoint, `LOOM_RUNTIME=opencode` in the global environment on robb-studio and loom-worker-2), **about 12% of every token spent went to scheduled role ticks that could not succeed**, and the daemon re-launched them every cycle all day. The sweeps on the same runtime were fine — 61 sweeps, 46 merged PRs.

Measured from OpenCode's own session store (`~/.loom/opt/opencode-*/xdg/data/opencode/opencode.db`, table `session`), which is the only complete record — the daemon's `LOOM_LAUNCH` line says `billing: not-measured` and robb-studio's daemon log prints no launch lines at all:

| host | role-tick sessions | tokens (in + out + cache) | OpenCode's cost estimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| loom-worker-2 | 780 | 149 M | $51 |
| robb-studio | 203 | 96 M | $35 |
| **total** | **983** | **~245 M (12% of 1.95 B)** | **~$86 of $532** |

(Friendli's meter for the same period read ~2.5 B tokens / ~$750, so the real cost of this slice is nearer $90–100.)

Two failure modes, both visible in worker-2's `~/.loom/daemon.log` for 2026-09-21, both repeated on every tick of every root:

1. **`cannot execute worker harness: Argument list too long (os error 7)` — 60 launches, judge and curator.** `worker_spawn/harness.rs:112` hands OpenCode the whole expanded prompt as one argv string (`command.args(["--", prompt])`). `worker_spawn/prompt.rs::expand` builds that string from the role's `.md` plus the repo's `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Linux caps a *single* argument at 128 KiB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`); judge/curator plus a canary's `CLAUDE.md` exceeds it, so `exec` fails in ~640 ms. These cost no tokens but each is logged, skipped, and retried next cycle ("has never completed a successful tick; logged and skipped, never fatal").
2. **`toolless launch: the opencode guarded binding never offered loom_read/loom_write/loom_edit/loom_bash` — 638 launches, doctor and champion (and the roles short enough to survive #1).** #8448 / PR #8482 (merged 07:09Z today) correctly classifies these as failed launches instead of successes — but a failed launch is still relaunched next tick. Each one spends ~13 s and a real model turn (`18 native event(s), 0 loom_* tool uses, 4 step_finish`) producing nothing. 616 of the 780 worker-2 role sessions exceeded 100 k tokens; the largest single Champion pass was 5.3 M.

The launches were admitted with `runtime-selection: <role> declares suggestedWorkerType="claude" in its role manifest but was admitted onto runtime="opencode" (selected by default-config)` on every one — the WARN from #6201 fired ~700 times and changed nothing, because `suggestedWorkerType` is documented as observability-only.

Nothing in `role_runner.rs` backs off a failing root: the only gate is the rate-limit cooldown (#4429). The dedup from #4349 downgrades the *log line* to DEBUG on repeats; the launch itself still happens.

## Candidate fixes (brainstorm — Curator to pick, or combine)

**A. Launch-failure circuit breaker per `(root, role, runtime)`.** After N (say 3) consecutive failures whose class is *launch* (exec error, exit 126/127, toolless per #8482, implausibly-fast exit-0) rather than *work*, skip that pair with exponential backoff — 15 min doubling to a 6 h ceiling — and reset on success, on a config/defaults change, or on daemon restart. The `LAST_ROLE_TICK` state and `consecutive_identical_failures` counter in `role_runner.rs` already exist; this adds a `next_attempt_at`. Cheapest, runtime-agnostic, and would have turned ~700 launches into ~30. Does not fix either root cause, so it must log loudly (one WARN per breaker trip, with the reason) and export a counter.

**B. Fix the E2BIG root cause: never pass the expanded prompt as argv.** Write it to a file under the worktree's `.loom/tmp/` (or a `memfd`/pipe) and pass a path or read it from stdin — OpenCode `run` accepts stdin when no positional prompt is given, and Pi has `--prompt-file`-style options to check. Add a pre-exec size check against `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` that fails with a *classified* config error ("prompt N KiB exceeds the 128 KiB single-argument limit; use …") rather than an OS error string. Necessary regardless of which other option lands; on its own it turns failure #1 into failure #2 (those ticks would then launch toolless).

**C. Capability pre-flight for native runtimes, cached per `(host, runtime, version)`.** Before admitting a *role* (not a sweep) onto `opencode`/`pi`, run a one-shot probe — e.g. spawn with a trivial prompt that must call `loom_read` on a fixture — and record whether the guarded tool binding is offered. Refuse admission (`runtime admission rejected: opencode 1.18.31 on this host has not passed the guarded-tools probe`) until it passes; re-probe on binary upgrade or by `loom-daemon validate --probe-runtimes`. Turns #8448's post-hoc detection into a pre-spend gate. Costs one small probe per host per version instead of 638 real turns.

**D. Scope a global runtime override to sweeps unless a role opts in.** Treat `LOOM_RUNTIME` / `runtimes.default` as applying to `sweep-lifecycle` (the thing #8436's metered-backstop design is about), and require an explicit `runtimes.roles.<role>` binding — or a manifest `suggestedWorkerType` that matches — before a *scheduled* role is admitted onto a native runtime. Upgrades the #6201 WARN from "loud" to "binding" for the scheduled-role case only. This is a semantics change to a documented knob (`runtime-adapters.md` § Runtime resolution), so it needs a config lint in `loom-daemon validate` that names every role the new rule would re-route, and a release note. It is the option that most directly encodes the operator's stated policy (subscription accounts for roles, metered endpoint as a sweep backstop).

**E. Per-runtime spend guard with no-outcome accounting.** Read OpenCode's session DB (it already has per-session `tokens_*`, `cost`, `model`, `directory`) and stop admitting work onto a metered runtime on a host once tokens spent by sessions that ended without a recorded outcome (no PR, no tool use, failed launch) exceed a configured daily budget. Broadest protection — it would also catch a future failure mode nobody has named yet — but the largest build, and it depends on the same DB-reading adapter that the missing fleet-feed model badge needs (`tokens_by_model` is Claude-transcript-only today), so it may be better as the follow-up that closes both gaps.

My ranking: **B is non-negotiable** (it is a plain bug), **A is the cheap general backstop**, and one of **C or D** decides whether the daemon *detects* an unusable runtime or *refuses to route roles there by default*. E is a separate issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- Replaying the 2026-09-21 worker-2 configuration (`LOOM_RUNTIME=opencode`, 40+ roots, judge/curator/doctor/champion roles, OpenCode 1.18.31) produces **no** `Argument list too long` exec failures; an oversized prompt is reported as a classified config error naming the limit.
- For any `(root, role, runtime)` whose launches fail for a launch-class reason, the number of launches is **bounded** (≤ 4 in the first hour, ≤ 8 in 24 h) and each skipped cycle is visible in `loom-daemon status`/telemetry with the reason and the next attempt time.
- Tokens spent by role ticks that end as failed launches, measured from the OpenCode session store, are **< 1%** of the host's total for the day (vs 12% observed).
- Every breaker trip / refused admission is a single WARN with the root, role, runtime, reason and remedy — not one line per tick.
- Existing sweeps on the same runtime are unaffected (46 merged PRs' worth of behaviour is the regression baseline).

## Evidence

- worker-2 `~/.loom/daemon.log` 2026-09-21T12:18Z onward: `LOOM_LAUNCH {"runtime":"opencode","provider":"friendli","model":"zai-org/GLM-5.3","profile":"friendli-glm",…}` followed by `cannot execute worker harness: Argument list too long (os error 7)`; `grep -c "toolless launch"` = 638.
- OpenCode session DB on both hosts, `select title, tokens_input+tokens_cache_read, tokens_output from session where title not like '%sweep%' order by 2 desc` — Champion passes at 2.7–5.3 M tokens each with zero tool use.
- Related: #8448 / #8482 (toolless detection), #6201 (`suggestedWorkerType` observability-only WARN), #8436 (ordered runtime preference / metered backstop), #6757 (never-succeeded vs regressed tick history), #4349 (repeat-failure log dedup).

title: Scheduled role ticks on the metered OpenCode runtime burned ~12% of the GLM-5.3 trial on launches that could never succeed (E2BIG prompt argv + toolless), relaunched every cycle
